tasks.short: Help site and department managers with cost questions, cost-centre allocations and their budget input.

today.trigger: A manager in Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo asks by mail or Teams about a cost, an allocation key or how to fill in the budget template.
steps: Read the question and find the cost centre and period in AFAS or the Power BI finance dashboard
Pull GL detail and headcount or flex hours into Excel
Work out the answer or the allocation (e.g. warehouse rent by m2, IT by FTE)
Write back to the manager or walk them through it in a Teams call
drudgery: Re-pulling the same GL extracts for each question
Explaining the same allocation keys every budget round
today.time_sinks: Hunting for the right extract and re-building small Excel models for one-off questions.

lenses.faster: A copilot on the prepared Power BI model answers the data part (which costs, which key, what last year was) in minutes; the analyst checks and adds the advice, cutting a typical question from about an hour to twenty minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous: a manager's question starts it, the copilot drafts the numbers and a short answer, and the analyst sends it.
lenses.ambitious: Give every site manager and shift lead a self-service budget helpdesk on certified definitions, so cost questions get answered the same day instead of waiting for the analyst; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses re-pulling GL extracts; the analyst wants more time on the conversation about what drives the cost.
lenses.options: For allocation questions, showing two or three allocation keys side by side (m2, FTE, pallets moved) changes which one the Finance Director picks.
lenses.altitude: The analyst spends less time fetching and more time owning allocation keys and cost definitions, with the right to decide which key applies; the job becomes more expert.
reach: Answer the Controller's cost-centre questions during close (needs GL mapping knowledge)
Support the HR Business Partners on staffing-cost questions (needs CAO pay scale basics)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the manager is really asking, which allocation is fair between sites, and how a number will land politically.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions vary and the advice involves judgement; the person stays the lead and the AI fetches and drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Manager question in Teams or mail
steps: Analyst asks the copilot in Power BI or Excel for the relevant cost lines and prior-year figures
Copilot returns numbers with the source table and a draft explanation
Analyst checks against AFAS and adjusts the advice
Analyst replies and files the answer in a shared FAQ on SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews every answer before it goes to the manager.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint FAQ list with question, answer and source query

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI answers questions and summarises reports on a prepared semantic model, but can misinterpret unprepared data and is English-only officially.
Finance executives report AI is least successful on tasks that demand human judgement.

risks: Copilot misreads Dutch field names or unprepared measures
Managers take a draft answer as policy
Answers in personal chatbots cannot be traced for the auditor
research_questions: How many cost questions a month come in, and how many repeat?
Does Noordhaven have Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity for Copilot?
Are allocation keys written down anywhere today?

tasks.short: Look at budget versus actual over months to spot trends that change next year's or the forecast's needs.

today.trigger: Monthly after close and during the forecast and budget cycle.
steps: Export actuals and budget by cost centre and site from AFAS or Power BI
Line up 12 to 24 months in Excel
Look for drift in fuel, flex labour, overtime, rent, energy
Ask site controllers or managers for explanations
Write a trend note for the Finance Director
drudgery: Aligning periods and cost-centre changes by hand
today.time_sinks: Data alignment and chasing the story behind each movement.

lenses.faster: Software lines up the series and flags trends; a model call drafts a driver note per site with the source lines, and the analyst spends time on checking and the explanations, roughly halving the work.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly refresh following close, the trend scan runs, a draft note per site is produced, and the analyst approves before it goes to the Finance Director.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly rolling forecast per site driven by defined drivers (orders, pallets, flex hours, fuel price), instead of a once-a-year budget; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses aligning periods in Excel; the analyst wants more time talking to site managers about why volumes and flex use move.
lenses.options: Two or three driver scenarios (e.g. peak season flex at 150 versus 300 workers) change the budget need itself.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns driver definitions and decides which trends go into the forecast; more expert work.
reach: Take over the People Analytics Analyst's flex-worker cost trend (needs agency portal data)
Feed the Controller's accrual estimates (needs close calendar knowledge)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which movement is a one-off (a lost client, a strike, a peak) and which is structural.
tasks.pattern_why: Trend detection is rule-based, but turning it into a driver note with sources is one checkable model step.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh after month close
steps: Scripted query aligns 24 months of actuals and budget by cost centre
Rules flag trends beyond a threshold
Model call drafts a driver note per site citing GL lines and agency hours
Analyst checks, adds context and approves
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves each note before release.
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned trend notes on SharePoint with source queries

evidence.claim: Forecasting nets +34 and variance analysis +28 in usefulness among finance executives.
Agents can gather data, do variance arithmetic and draft commentary while people decide.
Without defined drivers and clean data, AI makes existing errors harder to catch.

risks: Drivers not defined, so notes explain noise
Cost-centre restructures break the series
Commentary written after the number
research_questions: Are volume drivers (orders, pallets) available per site in a system?
How often did cost-centre structures change in the last two years?
Would the Finance Director use monthly site forecasts?

tasks.short: Each month, check department costs against budget and flag overspends to managers.

steps: Refresh the variance report per cost centre
Mark variances above the threshold
Look up invoices and agency hours behind each
Mail managers for explanations
Collect answers into the monthly pack
drudgery: Drilling into invoices one by one
today.time_sinks: Drill-down to transaction level and waiting for explanations.

lenses.faster: The variance table, threshold flags and drill-down to invoices run automatically; a model drafts the commentary, so the analyst only handles the flagged lines and reviews, cutting about 60%.
lenses.autonomous: Close completion triggers the variance run, managers get a pre-filled explanation request for their flagged lines, and the analyst handles exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly expenditure control for flex labour per site during peak season, when agency costs move fastest; demand would grow if cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses invoice-by-invoice drill-down; the analyst wants more time on the few variances that matter.
lenses.options: Little value in multiple drafts; the decision is whether to act on a variance.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets thresholds and control rules and decides which overspends go to the Finance Director; more expert.
reach: Check agency invoices against ordered hours for the Bookkeepers (needs agency contract terms)
Prepare the Controller's cost-accrual list (needs close process)

tasks.human_edge: Judging which overspend is a real control problem and handling the conversation with the manager.
tasks.pattern_why: Variance arithmetic and thresholds can be written down; only the commentary needs a model step.

in_practice.trigger: Month close status set in AFAS
steps: Script builds the variance table from the nightly extract
Rules flag variances above amount and percent thresholds with top transactions
Model call drafts a one-line explanation per flag
Managers confirm or correct in a form; analyst reviews exceptions
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews flagged variances and any manager disagreement before the pack is issued.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list of variances, explanations and sign-off

evidence.claim: For expenditure control and regular reports, deterministic checks with an llm_step for commentary are the suggested shape.
Agents flag records that do not tie and do variance arithmetic.

risks: Thresholds too tight create noise managers ignore
Nightly extract lag hides late postings
Draft explanations accepted without checking
research_questions: How many variances a month exceed today's threshold?
Can agency portals export hours automatically?
How quickly do managers answer today?

tasks.short: Check budget submissions from managers for gaps, errors and whether they follow our budget rules.

today.trigger: Budget or forecast templates come back from cost-centre owners.
steps: Collect Excel templates from SharePoint and mail
Check totals, missing lines and formulas
Check headcount and pay against CAO scales and flex rates
Compare to last year and to the guidance
Send back questions and corrections
drudgery: Checking broken formulas and missing cost lines
today.time_sinks: Many template versions and manual cross-checks.

lenses.faster: A validation script checks completeness, totals, CAO pay scale and agency rate rules on upload, so the analyst only reviews what failed, cutting about 55%.
lenses.autonomous: Upload to SharePoint triggers the checks; the submitter gets an issue list immediately; the analyst handles disputes and approves.
lenses.ambitious: Run the same checks on every monthly forecast update, not only the annual budget; demand grows if cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formula checking; the analyst wants more time challenging assumptions.
lenses.options: Not much; checks have one right answer.
lenses.altitude: The analyst writes and owns the budget rules and approves exceptions; more expert.
reach: Check pay assumptions with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist (needs CAO scale tables)
Validate headcount plans with HR Administrators (needs AVG handling of named data)

tasks.human_edge: Seeing an assumption that is technically valid but unrealistic, like a site planning no peak flex.
tasks.pattern_why: Completeness and conformance rules can be written down and run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Template uploaded to SharePoint budget folder
steps: Script reads the template and runs completeness and arithmetic checks
Rules compare pay and flex rates to CAO and agency tables
Issue list goes to submitter
Analyst reviews passed submissions and exceptions
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves each submission before it enters the master budget.
in_practice.logs_to: Check log per submission on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Checking estimates suits deterministic checks at autonomy 4.
Headcount plans with named people are personal data.

risks: Templates changed by users break the parser
Named headcount data mishandled under AVG
Rules not updated after a CAO change
research_questions: How many submissions and rounds per budget cycle?
Is the template locked and standard across sites?
Where are CAO scales held in machine-readable form?

tasks.short: Work out what money a new site project, client contract or initiative needs from records and data.

today.trigger: Management asks what a new client warehouse, extra shift, or system project would cost.
steps: Gather comparable actuals from AFAS by site
Get staffing, flex and equipment assumptions from operations and HR
Build a cost model in Excel
Check with the Controller and present the need
drudgery: Rebuilding the model structure each time
today.time_sinks: Collecting assumptions and history across systems.

lenses.faster: A model step pulls comparable site costs and drafts a resource model from a standard template with sources; the analyst sets assumptions and checks, saving about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: A request starts it, the draft model is built from history and drivers, and the analyst approves before it is shared.
lenses.ambitious: Offer the commercial team a cost estimate for every client tender within a day, a service sales does not get today; demand grows if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding model structure; the analyst wants more time testing assumptions with operations.
lenses.options: Scenarios (one or two shifts, own staff versus flex mix) change the decision itself.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the cost model library and the driver set and decides which assumptions apply; more expert.
reach: Cost recruitment needs with the Recruiters (needs time-to-hire data)
Estimate training costs for forklift and VCA with L&D (needs Studytube data)

tasks.human_edge: Judging operational assumptions and what a new client will really demand.
tasks.pattern_why: Turning scattered history into a structured, sourced draft model is one checkable step in a fixed flow.

in_practice.trigger: Request logged by management or sales
steps: Analyst enters scope (site, volume, shifts)
Script pulls comparable actuals and rates
Model call drafts the resource model and assumptions list with sources
Analyst adjusts and approves
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs off the model before it goes out.
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned model on SharePoint with assumption log

evidence.claim: Model building nets +27 and scenario planning +26 in usefulness.
Agents run scenario mechanics; people decide capital allocation.

risks: Comparable history is misleading for a new kind of client
Assumptions hidden inside the draft
Model built outside auditable tools
research_questions: How many such costings were done last year and how long did each take?
Would sales use a one-day tender cost estimate?
Is a standard model template accepted by the Finance Director?

tasks.short: Summarise budgets and give a recommendation on spending and investment requests.

today.trigger: A site or department submits an investment or extra budget request (e.g. forklifts, racking, extra flex).
steps: Read the request and supporting quotes
Check budget room and past spend
Calculate payback or cost impact in Excel
Write a recommendation memo for the Finance Director
today.time_sinks: Incomplete requests and writing the memo.

lenses.faster: A model step reads the request, checks budget room from the extract and drafts the memo with payback; the analyst checks and adds the recommendation, saving about 45%.
lenses.autonomous: A request on the SharePoint form triggers the draft; the analyst reviews and the Finance Director decides.
lenses.ambitious: Decide smaller requests (under a set amount) weekly instead of waiting for the monthly meeting; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reformatting; the analyst wants more time on the judgement in the recommendation.
lenses.options: Showing approve, defer, or lease-instead-of-buy changes the decision.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the request criteria and gets to decide small requests within a mandate; more expert.
reach: Check supplier quotes with Bookkeepers (needs AP vendor data)
Prepare bank covenant impact for the Finance Director (needs loan terms)

tasks.human_edge: Weighing strategic fit and the manager's track record; the decision stays human.
tasks.pattern_why: One call turns a messy request into a structured memo inside a fixed approval workflow.

steps: Script fetches budget room and past spend
Model call drafts memo with summary, numbers and options
Analyst checks and writes recommendation
Finance Director decides
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves memo; Finance Director decides funding.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint request list with memo and decision

evidence.claim: Budgeting is where finance executives most often found AI more useful than expected (+42).
Funds requests: an llm_step drafts a recommendation memo; a person decides.

risks: Draft recommendation anchors the decision
Quotes misread
Approval trail not audit-proof
research_questions: How many requests a month and of what size?
Would the Finance Director delegate small approvals?
Are investment criteria written down?

tasks.short: Organise the monthly budget pack and ad hoc reports for the board, sites and the bank.

today.trigger: Month end, quarter end, or a special request from the board or Rabobank.
steps: Refresh Power BI and Excel reports
Gather commentary from site controllers
Assemble PowerPoint pack
Check consistency and send out

lenses.faster: The pack is generated from certified Power BI reports with drafted commentary; the analyst edits and checks, saving about half.
lenses.autonomous: Close completion triggers the pack build; the analyst approves before release.
lenses.ambitious: A short site-level pack for each of the three site managers every month, a group not served today; demand would grow but watch report creep.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copy-paste of charts; the analyst wants more time on the story for the board.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns report definitions and decides what goes in; less assembly, more editorial judgement.
reach: Take over the HR dashboard commentary from People Analytics (needs HR KPI definitions)
Prepare the Controller's close summary (needs close checklist)

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the message for the board and bank and answering their questions.
tasks.pattern_why: Report generation from a fixed model is rule-based; commentary is a small model step.

steps: Power BI refresh and paginated report export
Script builds pack
Model drafts commentary
Analyst edits and approves
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst and Finance Director approve before distribution.

evidence.claim: The most AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting.
Copilot in Power BI summarises reports on Fabric F2+ or Premium.

risks: More reports requested because they are cheap
Commentary errors reach the bank
English-only Copilot for Dutch readers
research_questions: How many hours does the monthly pack take today?
Which reports are actually read?
Is the semantic model certified?

tasks.short: Tie cost-centre budgets to site and company totals, including the contingency reserve.

today.trigger: Budget round, reforecast, or a budget shift between cost centres.
steps: Map cost-centre budgets to site and division totals
Check sums tie to the approved company budget
Track draws on contingency
Update the master file

lenses.faster: A rules-based hierarchy and tie-out check in the budget model removes manual mapping; the analyst reviews breaks, saving about 60%.
lenses.autonomous: Any budget change triggers the tie-out; the analyst handles breaks and approves contingency draws.
lenses.ambitious: Daily visibility on contingency use per site during peak season; modest extra demand.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses tie-outs; the analyst wants more time on whether reserves are the right size.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the budget hierarchy and transfer rules; more control, less clerical work.
reach: Maintain cost-centre master data with the Controller (needs AFAS admin rights)
Support the Accountant's budget load into AFAS

tasks.human_edge: Deciding on contingency draws and transfers between sites.
tasks.pattern_why: Hierarchy mapping and tie-outs are fixed rules.

steps: Script applies the cost-centre hierarchy
Tie-out checks against approved totals
Breaks and contingency draws listed
Analyst approves
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves transfers; Finance Director approves contingency draws above a limit.
in_practice.logs_to: Transfer and tie-out log on SharePoint

evidence.claim: The O*NET appropriations tasks map to cost-centre and site budgets at a private company.
Allocations suit deterministic checks at autonomy 4.

risks: Hierarchy out of date after reorganisation
Uncontrolled transfers
Auditor cannot trace changes
research_questions: How often do budget transfers happen?
Is there a formal contingency reserve per site?
Is the cost-centre hierarchy maintained in AFAS?

role.altitude: From assembling budgets and packs to owning the driver set, cost definitions, allocation keys and forecast rules, with a mandate to decide small funds requests and set control thresholds.
reach: Flex-worker cost trends from People Analytics
Agency invoice checks with Bookkeepers
Close summaries and accrual lists for the Controller
Tender cost estimates for sales
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality in the nightly AFAS extract, undefined volume drivers, Power BI capacity and English-only Copilot; judgement on assumptions, board and bank conversations stay human.
skills_to_grow: Power BI semantic modelling and DAX
Operational knowledge of warehouse and transport costs
role.ambitious_version: A monthly rolling forecast and scenarios per site, with self-service cost answers for site managers and one-day tender costings for sales.
